input.quote: 12.4 Customer shall not solicit, hire, or employ any Vendor employee during the term or for twenty-four months afterward, regardless of how the employee applies.
input.rationale: § 12.4 binds only Customer with a no-hire (not merely non-solicit) covering all Vendor employees for 24 months post-term, expressly including employees who apply on their own initiative — i.e., no general-advertising or unsolicited-approach carve-out. That hits the walk-away triggers (no-hire, all personnel, 24 months) and contradicts § 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no no-hire commitment and may hire anyone responding to general recruitment. Preferred position is no non-solicit on Customer, so we delete § 12.4; the comment offers the fallback (mutual, involved personnel only, 12 months, standard carve-outs, no no-hire).

proposal.summary: Delete the one-way 24-month no-hire binding Customer (§ 12.4)
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have deleted § 12.4: it imposes a one-way, 24-month no-hire on us covering all Vendor employees "regardless of how the employee applies", which we do not accept and which directly contradicts § 12.3 (Customer has made no no-hire commitment and may hire anyone responding to general recruitment). If Vendor needs protection, we can accept a mutual non-solicitation limited to personnel directly involved in the Services for 12 months after their involvement ends, with carve-outs for general advertisements and unsolicited approaches and no no-hire element.
